overview: Neovenator salerii is the most completely known large theropod from the United Kingdom, discovered on the Isle of Wight in the Wessex Formation (Barremian, ~130 Ma). At around 7.5 metres it was the apex predator of the Early Cretaceous Wessex ecosystem, which also included Baryonyx, Iguanodon and Hypsilophodon.

Originally described as an allosauroid, Neovenator is now placed within Neovenatoridae — a clade of large tetanuran theropods with Gondwanan affinities that includes Megaraptor and possibly Australovenator. Its discovery substantially broadened knowledge of European Early Cretaceous predator diversity beyond the spinosaurid-only picture that had previously prevailed.

fossilSites.name: Wessex Formation
fossilSites.note: Barremian fluvial and overbank deposits yielding the most complete Neovenator specimen alongside Iguanodon, Baryonyx and Hypsilophodon.

articles.title: Discovery
articles.body: Found by the Salero family in a landslip on the Isle of Wight in 1978, the specimen was sold to Dinosaur Farm Museum before being formally described by Hutt and colleagues in 1996. The species name honours the Salero family. Much of the skull and most of the postcranium are represented.

articles.title: Anatomy and classification
articles.body: The skull has a relatively long, low profile with large fenestrae (openings) reducing skull weight. The forelimbs are robust with large claws. Originally placed in Allosauridae, phylogenetic analysis now consistently recovers Neovenator in Neovenatoridae — a clade with probable Gondwanan origins that dispersed to Europe and possibly North America.

articles.title: Isle of Wight ecosystem
articles.body: The Wessex Formation records a complex floodplain system with channels, swamps and dryland patches in a warm sub-tropical climate. Neovenator would have hunted Iguanodon herds and possibly Polacanthus (a nodosaurid ankylosaur). Its co-occurrence with Baryonyx suggests two large predators used different microhabitats — Neovenator on open land, Baryonyx near water.

fossilRecord.formations: Wessex Formation, Isle of Wight, England
fossilRecord.material: A near-complete skeleton — the most complete large theropod from Britain.
fossilRecord.paleo: Early Cretaceous river delta and floodplain environment of what is now southern England.
fossilRecord.evidence: Large theropod anatomy with features linking it to carcharodontosaurids or megaraptorans — its exact placement is still debated.

record.description: Neovenator salerii was a large allosauroid theropod from the Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, known from one relatively complete partial skeleton with skull and postcranial material.
facts: The holotype and associated discoveries preserve substantial cranial, vertebral, girdle and limb anatomy.
Its placement as a basal carcharodontosaurian is common, while the content of Neovenatoridae varies among analyses.
Pathologies are present in the type, but stories about their causes or survival are inferential.

review.ageReviewNote: The Wessex Formation type horizon is Barremian, approximately 130-125 Ma.
